mechanic: One event told at two times (an event that happens once): two honest witnesses time a shot by two clocks, and the clash is on the timeline before anyone is accused. The time that cannot stand is the slow clock's, and with it goes an alibi.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose (docs/authored-stories.md, outline A). `frame` is what the narrator's own prose always carries; `clues` are the units that could be case files. `facts` names the world model's facts that realise a clue.

frame.says: A shot was fired through the window of Sir Giles's study that evening.

rules_out.a quarter to nine: c.stable_clock: the gardener read the stable clock (c.gardener), and it is a quarter of an hour slow; c.hall_clock: the clock the housemaid counted was right

questions.asks: Was Mr. Royle still in the library when the shot was fired?

rules_out.yes: c.evening: he left at ten to nine by the hall clock; c.maid: the shot came at nine by the same clock

clues.says: Mr. Royle sat with the narrator in the library until ten to nine by the hall clock.

clues.source: Susan, the housemaid, to the narrator
clues.says: The shot came as the hall clock struck nine; she counted the strokes.

clues.source: Bowker, the gardener, to the narrator
clues.says: The shot was at a quarter to nine; he looked at the stable clock the moment he heard it.
The narrator set the hall clock that morning by the church clock.

clues.source: The narrator's own look next morning
clues.says: The stable clock is a quarter of an hour slow.
